memos.headline: S04 leads with dominant relative strength; S06 and S07 break down below 50d means
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. S04 is the standout leader—up 33.4% over 12 weeks with +29.7% relative strength vs SPY, RSI at 67.5 (strong but not yet overbought), and only 1.3% off its 52-week high; the trend is powerful and intact. S09 is the second-best setup with 12w relative strength of +12.0% vs SPY, sitting just 1.5% off highs with RSI 64.2, though the 26w return of only +3.4% suggests this is a newer trend that needs monitoring. On the weak side, S07 is deeply damaged at -24.8% drawdown from its 52-week high, trading essentially at its 200d mean, with 12w relative strength of -12.5% vs SPY and high volatility (ATR 3.17%)—this is a broken chart. S06 is also deteriorating, trading 4.9% below its 50d mean with RSI at 38.3 and 4w relative strength of -8.4%, signaling distribution. I would reconsider my S04 long below 500 (roughly the 50d mean area) and my S07 avoid if it reclaims 870.

views.note: Strongest 12w relative strength in the universe at +29.7% vs SPY, near highs with RSI 67.5; would reassess on a close below 500.
Near 52w highs with 12w rel strength +12.0% vs SPY and RSI 64.2; trend is intact but 26w return of only +3.4% warrants watching for sustainability.
Healthy uptrend with +13.4% above 200d mean, moderate RSI 53, and positive 4w/12w relative strength vs SPY; drawdown of -4.2% is manageable.
Strong 26w return of +30% but 12w relative strength vs SPY is -2.7%, suggesting momentum is fading relative to the market despite being near highs.
Bouncing with +4.4% 1w return but still -9.6% from highs and 12w relative strength is -3.9% vs SPY; needs to clear 167 to confirm trend repair.
Down 10.4% over 12 weeks with -14.1% relative strength vs SPY, below 50d mean, RSI 49.4 and -13.1% drawdown—classic distribution pattern.
Trading 4.9% below 50d mean with RSI 38.3 and 4w relative strength of -8.4% vs SPY; trend has clearly broken down.
Worst drawdown in the universe at -24.8% from highs, flat to 200d mean, 12w rel strength -12.5% vs SPY with 3.17% ATR—broken and volatile.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Lead on Explosive Earnings Growth; S09 and S01 Flash Margin and Growth Warnings
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe. S10 stands out with 106% YoY revenue growth to $96.2B and a 62% net margin, while S05 posted a 93.7% net margin on $119.8B of revenue with net income up nearly 298% YoY—both names exhibit durable, high-quality earnings power with modest debt loads ($33.4B and $14.8B respectively). On the other end, S09 delivered only 2.4% revenue growth with net income down 45.8% YoY and a thin 4.9% margin, and S01 saw net income decline 15.8% on essentially flat revenue of $21.2B with $29.3B in debt—neither name shows the earnings trajectory I want to own. I would change my view on S09 if Q2 margins recover above 8% and revenue growth re-accelerates, and on S01 if net income stabilizes and debt-to-equity improves materially.

views.note: Revenue doubling YoY to $96.2B with a 62% net margin and only $33.4B debt is the best fundamental profile in this universe.
A 93.7% net margin on $119.8B revenue with minimal debt ($14.8B) and 298% net income growth is extraordinary earnings power.
Full-year revenue of $90B growing 17.7% with a 39.7% net margin and manageable $40.3B debt reflects durable, high-margin compounding.
Revenue of $200.6B (+19.6% YoY) and net income up 245% show strong operating leverage, though $133B in debt warrants monitoring.
24% revenue growth and 65% net income growth to a 17.5% margin are solid, but $36.2B debt on $20.5B quarterly revenue keeps conviction moderate.
Strong 27.7% revenue growth and 36.9% margin are offset by an outsized $460.5B debt load that compresses financial flexibility.
Solid 16.4% revenue growth and 27.2% margin, but $82.3B in debt and slower earnings acceleration versus peers keep me neutral.
Revenue essentially flat at $112B with a 4.9% net margin; the 61% net income bounce is off a low base and margin remains thin.
Net income fell 45.8% YoY on anemic 2.4% revenue growth with a 4.9% margin—clear cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for.
Revenue grew only 1.5% while net income declined 15.8% and debt sits at $29.3B, signaling deteriorating earnings power.

memos.headline: Stagflationary Tilt: 3.4% CPI and 5.24% 10y Yield Argue Against Duration and Cyclicals
memos.body: I see a macro regime that is best described as a hawkish pause turning into a mild re-tightening: the fed funds upper bound has risen 25bp over three months to 4.00%, while 12-month CPI is running at 3.4% — well above target — and the 10y yield has surged 110bp year-over-year to 5.24%. The labor market is stable with unemployment flat at 4.20% over three months and actually down 20bp year-over-year, so there is no imminent recession signal to force the Fed's hand toward easing. The 10y-2y spread at +47bp is mildly positive and steepening, consistent with the market pricing in persistent inflation and higher term premia rather than imminent cuts. This combination of sticky inflation, a resilient labor market, and sharply higher long rates is toxic for duration-sensitive growth equities and supportive for banks (wider NIM from steeper curve) and energy (inflation hedge). A September CPI print below 3.0% or a sudden jump in unemployment above 4.5% would flip my regime call toward easing expectations.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth names face severe headwinds from the 110bp YoY surge in the 10y yield to 5.24% and no near-term easing catalyst.
High-multiple growth is pressured by rising real rates; the Fed hiked 25bp over three months with inflation still at 3.4%.
Banks benefit from a steepening curve (10y-2y +12bp over 3m to 0.47pp) and higher absolute rate levels boosting net interest margins.
Energy acts as an inflation hedge in a 3.4% CPI environment with stable employment and no recession signal.
Staples offer defensive positioning but their bond-proxy character is a drag when the 10y yield is at 5.24%; net neutral.
Cyclicals face margin pressure from higher borrowing costs and a Fed that is not easing despite stable unemployment at 4.2%.
Uncertain sector exposure; stable labor market is supportive but rising rates cap upside — staying neutral until regime clarity improves.

memos.headline: S10 Positive Momentum Stands Out; S03 and S08 Leadership Turnover Warrants Caution
memos.body: I see the clearest sentiment signal in S10, which posted strong results in late August driving an +8.7% price reaction, followed by a new material agreement and additional Other Events disclosure—three 8-Ks in under three weeks suggests an active narrative that remains constructive. S03 had two 8-Ks in quick succession including a director/officer departure and an Other Events filing, which together create an uncertain tone around leadership stability. S08's amended 8-K/A on officer changes is a lagging disclosure that may already be priced but keeps sentiment murky. S07's entry into a material definitive agreement and new financial obligation on Sep 1 is a potential narrative shift worth monitoring, though I lack tone data to gauge market reception with high confidence. For S04 and S02, the Reg FD disclosures are routine investor-relations events that I read as sentiment-neutral absent further context.

views.note: Three 8-Ks in three weeks including a strong +8.7% earnings reaction suggest positive sentiment momentum that may not yet be fully priced.
Back-to-back filings including a leadership departure create an unsettled narrative that tilts tone negative.
Amended officer-change disclosure is stale by now and likely already absorbed by the market.
New material agreement and direct financial obligation could shift sentiment either way; insufficient tone data to take a directional view.
Reg FD disclosure is standard investor-relations activity with no discernible sentiment shift.
Single Reg FD filing provides no meaningful tone signal.

memos.headline: Surging Oil and Policy Uncertainty Signal Geopolitical Stress; Energy-Exposed Names Face Divergent Risk
memos.body: I am seeing a sharp divergence between equity-implied volatility (VIX at 15.41, down 8.8% over 3m) and the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index, which has spiked 60.5% over three months to 305—a level historically associated with active sanctions regimes or major trade-policy shifts. WTI crude at $98.26 is up 31.8% over three months, consistent with supply-side disruption or tightening energy-security policy rather than demand-pull; high-yield OAS widening (+45bp over 3m to 3.15%) corroborates rising credit stress in energy-importing sectors. The combination of elevated policy uncertainty and surging oil prices without a commensurate VIX spike suggests markets are pricing geopolitical risk into commodities and credit but not yet into equities broadly—a gap I expect to close. I have moderate conviction that energy producers and defense-adjacent names benefit structurally, while companies with concentrated supply chains or high energy-input costs face headwinds; a reversal in sanctions or a credible ceasefire would change my view.

views.note: Recent 8.01 Other Events filing on 2026-09-14 lacks detail, but elevated oil and policy uncertainty warrant monitoring for supply-chain or regulatory exposure.
Reg FD disclosure in early September provides no clear geopolitical catalyst; I stay neutral pending clarity on how the 31.8% oil surge and widening HY spreads affect its cost structure.
Two 8-K filings in quick succession (Aug-Sep) amid a 60.5% jump in policy uncertainty and surging oil prices raise the risk of adverse regulatory or supply-chain developments.
Reg FD disclosure on 2026-09-08 coincides with the early phase of the oil and uncertainty spike; without further detail, I cannot distinguish structural benefit from transient noise.
With WTI near $98 and policy uncertainty at 305, energy-security beneficiaries should see structural tailwinds; I favor S06 as a proxy absent disconfirming filings.
High-yield OAS widening of 48bp in one month and surging energy costs create a hostile backdrop for leveraged or energy-intensive names without clear hedging.
